# Evaluation

## Methodology

* **Datasets**
  * **Seed (bundled)** — 6,000 synthetic URLs and 6,000 synthetic DOM feature rows generated by
    `ml/generate_seed.py` (deterministic). Exists so the system works out of the box with no
    downloads. **Not suitable for reporting results** — templates make it far easier than real data.
  * **PhiUSIIL Phishing URL Dataset** (UCI, 2024; 235,795 URLs, 134,850 legitimate / 100,945
    phishing, with URL and HTML features; CC BY 4.0). Primary dataset for the report.
    Note PhiUSIIL labels legitimate = 1; PhishNetra flips it so phishing is the positive class.
* **Split** — stratified 80/20 train/test, `random_state=42`, shared by training and evaluation
  (`ml/datasets.py`). Optional 5-fold stratified CV on the training split (`--cv`).
* **Leakage control** — the URL model is trained only on the raw URL string with PhishNetra's own
  features. PhiUSIIL's precomputed `URLSimilarityIndex`, `TLDLegitimateProb` etc. are *not* used,
  because they are near-perfect separators derived from the labels' source lists.
* **Metrics** — accuracy, precision, recall, F1, ROC-AUC, PR-AUC, false-positive rate, confusion
  matrix (`ml/common.py::metrics`). Plots (ROC + confusion matrix) go to `ml/reports/*.png`.
* **Ablation** — `ml/evaluate.py` runs the test split through the *real* layers and policy engine
  with different layer subsets enabled, reporting metrics at both operating points: flagged
  (risk ≥ WARN = 30) and blocked (risk ≥ BLOCK = 75). Reputation runs offline (no WHOIS/TLS) so
  results are reproducible.

## Reproduce

```bash
python ml/download_datasets.py --phiusiil            # ~55 MB from archive.ics.uci.edu
python ml/train_url_model.py --data phiusiil --cv
python ml/train_dom_model.py --data phiusiil
python ml/evaluate.py --data phiusiil --sample 20000  # all 4 layers incl. DOM
```

Outputs: `ml/reports/url_model_phiusiil.{json,png}`, `dom_model_phiusiil.{json,png}`,
`ablation_phiusiil.{json,png}`.

## Results on the bundled seed data (sanity check only)

Component models (test split, n = 1,200):

| Model | Accuracy | Precision | Recall | F1 | ROC-AUC |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| URL ensemble (L2) | 0.9967 | 0.9983 | 0.9950 | 0.9967 | 1.0000 |
| DOM random forest (L3) | 0.9942 | 0.9917 | 0.9967 | 0.9942 | 0.9999 |

URL-stage ablation through the policy engine (test split, n = 1,200):

| Layers | ROC-AUC | Precision@WARN | Recall@WARN | F1@WARN | FPR@WARN | Recall@BLOCK | FPR@BLOCK |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Reputation only | 0.852 | 1.000 | 0.552 | 0.711 | 0.000 | 0.000 | 0.000 |
| Brand only | 0.862 | 1.000 | 0.723 | 0.840 | 0.000 | 0.443 | 0.000 |
| URL model only | 1.000 | 0.997 | 0.998 | 0.998 | 0.003 | 0.988 | 0.000 |
| URL + reputation | 1.000 | 0.998 | 0.998 | 0.998 | 0.002 | 0.552 | 0.000 |
| **Rep + URL + brand (URL stage)** | **1.000** | **1.000** | **0.998** | **0.999** | **0.000** | **0.850** | **0.000** |

Interpretation: fusing layers removes the URL model's residual false positives (FPR 0.003 → 0)
while keeping recall. Block recall is deliberately lower than flag recall: by policy, a statistical
model alone can only WARN; BLOCK needs decisive (blocklist / brand-spoof) or corroborated evidence.
That trade (fewer hard blocks, zero blocked false positives) is the intended zero-trust behaviour;
`backend/config.yaml` exposes the thresholds to explore it.

> ⚠ Replace these tables with the PhiUSIIL numbers for the final report. Seed scores are
> inflated because the synthetic generator's templates are learnable.

## Latency (measured locally, macOS, Python 3.9)

| Path | Typical |
|---|---|
| Allowlisted / cached domain | 5–40 ms |
| Unknown domain, URL stage (WHOIS + TLS in parallel, 1.2 s budget) | 0.2–1.2 s |
| DOM stage (WHOIS cached by then) | 20–100 ms |
| Blocklisted domain (declarativeNetRequest) | ~0 ms, before the request is sent |
| URL model inference | < 1 ms per URL |

## Limitations / threats to validity

* Seed data is synthetic; DOM features from the extension are computed on the live DOM, PhiUSIIL's
  on raw HTML, so `LineOfCode`-style counts differ slightly (distribution shift).
* `DomainTitleMatchScore` / `URLTitleMatchScore` are re-implemented approximations of PhiUSIIL's
  definitions.
* PhiUSIIL legitimate URLs are mostly bare home pages while phishing URLs often have paths; URL
  models can partly learn "has a path". Evaluate on an independent recent feed (e.g. a fresh
  OpenPhish + Tranco sample) to measure generalisation and temporal drift.
* Typosquat detection (edit distance 1) can flag legitimate look-alike words (e.g. `apply` vs
  `apple`); the policy caps a lone brand signal of 85 at WARN.
* WHOIS availability varies by TLD; missing age data is treated as "no evidence", not as risk.
